passages.note: Her Aye on concurrence is a recorded act, but the bill regulates local parking mandates on private development rather than allocating transportation investment.

passages.provision_quote: A public agency shall not impose or enforce any minimum automobile parking requirement on a residential, commercial, or other development project if the project is located within one-half mile of public transit.
passages.note: The operative section bars public agencies from imposing parking minimums near transit; it directs no transportation spending and names no investment priority.

rows.reasoning: The only act on file is her Aye on AB 2097 (2021-2022), whose operative section provides that "A public agency shall not impose or enforce any minimum automobile parking requirement on a residential, commercial, or other development project if the project is located within one-half mile of public transit." That removes a local regulatory mandate on private developers; it does not say whether government should focus investment on "pedestrian infrastructure, cycling networks, and public transit over new road capacity" or on "road capacity and traffic flow," which is the dimension these rungs separate. Nothing here evidences a rung, including the parking clause of "Prioritize highway access and abundant free parking as the foundation of local transportation policy," which is about the foundation of local transportation policy rather than a parking-minimum mandate.
